objectives: Explain the ways in which ownership of real estate is acquired.
Apply the pre-emption right of co-owners in a sale of a share.
Distinguish a building right, a right of use and a servitude, and say how each ends.
Explain acquisition by prescription and why it matters for the circumstantial verification.
Explain what the entry of a deed protects against, and the effect of a recorded claim.

cards.front: Name three ways to acquire ownership.
cards.back: Legal transaction, prescription, other ways in law such as inheritance ([[zs:77]]).
**10 years** of uninterrupted possession; **5 years** in good faith ([[zs:79]]).
Loss of possession for more than **six months** ([[zs:81]]).
Possession: control as **one's own**. Holding: control **not** as one's own, e.g. a tenant ([[zs:68]]).
They are **presumed equal** until the contrary is proven ([[zs:30]]).

cards.front: What must a co-owner present to the notary before selling a share to a third person?
cards.back: Written evidence of an **offer to the other co-owners on the same terms** and a written declaration that **no one accepted** ([[zs:33]]).

cards.front: Time limit for a co-owner's redemption claim?
Form of a voluntary partition of real estate?
cards.back: Written with **notarially certified signatures**; court permission if persons without capacity or absent persons take part ([[zs:35]]).

cards.front: Can common parts of a condominium be divided?
A building right of 2019 was never used. May the holder start building in 2026?
cards.back: **No.** The right to build on another's land lapses after **5 years** of non-use ([[zs:67]]).

cards.front: Material interest for a building right deed?
cards.back: **90%** of the market price of the land ([[znnd:96:2]]).

cards.front: A father kept a right of use after a gift and then lived in a care home for six years. What happened to the right?
cards.back: It **lapsed**: a right of use ends when it is not exercised for **5 years** ([[zs:59]]). It also cannot be sold ([[zs:56|Art. 56]]).

cards.front: When does a right of use end?
cards.back: Death of the holder (unless shorter term), end of a legal entity, loss of the thing, **5 years** of non-use ([[zs:59]]).

cards.front: Form of a waiver of ownership of real estate?
cards.back: Written with **notarially certified signature**, and **entered** in the property register ([[zs:100]]).

cards.front: The seller sold the same flat twice; the second buyer entered first. Who owns it?
cards.back: The **second** buyer: an unentered act cannot be opposed to a third person who acquired from the same owner and **entered** first ([[zs:113]]).

quiz.question: A person has possessed a house in good faith on the basis of a defective deed for 6 years without interruption. What is the position?
options: Ownership by prescription: five years suffice in good faith
No ownership yet; ten years are needed in every case
No ownership; possession never replaces a deed for real estate
No ownership yet; twenty years are needed for a house
quiz.explanation: [[zs:79]]: a good-faith possessor acquires real estate by five years of uninterrupted possession; otherwise ten years. Good faith means possession on a legal ground capable of making the possessor the owner, without knowledge of its defect ([[zs:70|Art. 70]]). Twenty years is not a term of the act.

quiz.question: Three siblings own a house. Nothing proves the shares. What does the law presume?
options: Equal shares of 1/3 each
The shares stated by the oldest sibling
Shares in proportion to the age of each sibling
No presumption; a court sets the shares
quiz.explanation: [[zs:30]]: the shares of co-owners are presumed equal until the contrary is proven. A deed or a certificate of heirs can prove other shares; age and seniority prove nothing.

quiz.question: A co-owner wants to sell her share to a stranger. What does the notary require from her?
options: Proof of an offer to the co-owners and a declaration of refusal
The written consent of the other co-owners to the sale
A permission of the district court for the sale of a share to a stranger
A valuation of the share by a licensed appraiser
quiz.explanation: [[zs:33]]: before selling a share to a third person, the co-owner presents written evidence that the share was offered to the other co-owners on the same terms and declares in writing that none of them accepted. Their consent is not needed: the offer and its refusal suffice; a false declaration opens the redemption claim.

quiz.question: A co-owner sold his share to a third person with a false declaration. Within what time can another co-owner sue to redeem it?
options: Two months from the sale
One year from the sale
Five years from the sale
Six months from the sale
quiz.explanation: [[zs:33]]: the claim for redemption is filed within two months of the sale; the co-owner who wins must pay within one month after the decision becomes final, or the decision is void by law.

quiz.question: A building right was granted in 2018. Construction never started. What is the position in 2026?
options: The right lapsed; it was not used for five years
The right is still valid; it has no time limit
The right turned into ownership of the land
The right lapses only after ten years of non-use
quiz.explanation: [[zs:67]]: the right to build on another's land lapses when it is not exercised for five years. 2018 plus five years ended in 2023; the land stays with its owner.

quiz.question: Parents donate their flat to their son and keep a life-long right of use. Who pays the property tax while the parents live there?
options: The parents, as holders of the right of use
The son, as the owner of the flat
Both, in equal parts, as the law presumes for spouses
Nobody, because the flat is a family home
quiz.explanation: [[zs:57]]: the holder of the right of use pays the costs of use, including taxes and fees. The owner of the bare ownership pays nothing while the right lasts; the Local Taxes Act says the same for the property tax ([[zmdt:11:3]]).

quiz.question: May the holder of a right of use sell that right to a third person?
options: No; the holder cannot transfer the right
Yes, with a notarial deed and an entry
Yes, with the written consent of the owner
Yes, but only to relatives in the direct line
quiz.explanation: [[zs:56]]: the holder of a right of use may not transfer it; the right is personal and ends with the holder's death ([[zs:59|Art. 59]]). No consent or form changes that.

quiz.question: Which form does a voluntary partition of a plot between two co-owners need?
options: Written with notarially certified signatures
A notarial deed issued by the notary of the district
Simple written form, signed by both
An oral agreement before two witnesses
quiz.explanation: [[zs:35]]: a voluntary partition of real estate needs written form with notarially certified signatures; persons without capacity or absent persons need court permission. In practice offices make a partition contract certified and entered ([[pv:4]]).

quiz.question: An owner wants to waive ownership of a ruined barn. When is the waiver effective?
options: When written with a certified signature and entered
When announced in writing to the municipality and the cadastre
When the owner stops paying the property tax
When signed in simple writing before a witness
quiz.explanation: [[zs:100]]: a waiver of ownership of real estate takes effect only when made in writing with a notarially certified signature and entered in the property register; until the entry the owner may withdraw it.

quiz.question: A seller sold the same flat to A on Monday and to B on Tuesday. B's deed was entered first. Who is protected?
options: B, who entered first
A, who bought first
Both, in equal shares
The seller decides
quiz.explanation: [[zs:113]]: until entry, an act cannot be relied upon against third persons who acquired rights from the same owner and entered them earlier. B entered first and wins; A keeps only a claim for damages against the seller.

quiz.question: A buyer of a car from a person who was not the owner acted in good faith. Did the buyer become the owner?
options: No; a car transfer needs certified signatures
Yes; good faith always suffices for movables of any kind
Yes; after six months of possession
Yes; if the price paid was a fair one
quiz.explanation: [[zs:78]]: good-faith acquisition of a movable from a non-owner does not apply when the transfer needs a notarial deed or notarially certified signatures; a car needs certified signatures ([[zdvp:144:2]]). Movables are otherwise acquired by prescription in five years ([[zs:80|Art. 80]]).

quiz.question: The owners of the four flats in a small building want to divide the yard into four fenced gardens by a contract. Is that possible?
options: No; the common parts cannot be divided
Yes; with a partition contract with certified signatures
Yes; with the consent of three quarters of the owners
Yes; if the municipality approves the four gardens
quiz.explanation: [[zs:38]]: the common parts of a condominium, including the land and the yard, cannot be divided. The owners may agree on the use of the yard, but each flat keeps its ideal part of the common parts ([[zs:40|Art. 40]]).
